chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Musa from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from his father from Ali ibn Uqba from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri from al-'Ala' ibn Sayyabah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The testimony of the player of Nard (dice) and the fourteen (gamblers) and the owner of the two dice is not accepted. He says: No, by Allah, and Yes, by Allah. He died, by Allah, is a witness, and was killed, by Allah, is a witness, even if he neither died nor was killed.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the testimony of gamblers not accepted in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that habitual gamblers are legally disqualified as witnesses (*mawdu' al-shahadah*) due to the trivialization of divine oaths in their daily speech. This principle highlights the Shia jurisprudential link between moral integrity (*adalah*) and legal reliability, where frequent casual swearing erodes the solemnity required for testimony.
